title: Resume changes from recorded work context
statement: The system shall maintain and return a current structured handoff for each active Change so another authorized participant can identify an appropriate next action without the originating conversation or reconstructing activity history.

what.problem: A new participant may have access to engineering definitions but lack the recorded state, ownership, outstanding issues, or next action needed to resume an interrupted Change.
what.desired_outcome: An authorized participant can determine what remains to be done from the retained Change context and can recognize gaps without treating a suggested action as permission.

why.rationale: Preserving engineering definitions alone does not tell a new participant what work remains or how to continue a controlled Change.

stakeholders: Engineers and engineering agents handing off or resuming work
Reviewers and project decision owners responsible for outstanding decisions

conditions: When work on an in-progress Change is interrupted or handed to another participant, while the recorded context remains in the governed scope.

contexts: In the current authoritative Change context and the current engineering records it references.

how.approach: Retain the common resumption context with the Change and reference each activity's authoritative subjects and applicable basis revisions. Authoring context identifies affected definitions, derivation sources, decisions made, unresolved analysis, and proposed edits. Implementation context identifies the governing requirements and design, assigned work, changed realization, completed and remaining work, and relevant verification obligations. Verification context identifies the requirements and exact subjects assessed, assessment procedure and conditions, planned checks, actual execution state, observed results or failures, evidence locations, and remaining checks. Review context identifies the exact reviewed subjects, governing review basis, findings and their disposition or correction owner, unresolved decisions, and the next review or correction action. Reference facts at their authoritative owner rather than maintaining independent copies. Distinguish intended verification from observed evidence, and expose missing, conflicting, stale, or inapplicable context explicitly without inventing an action or authority.

how_much.scope: Covers explicitly recorded Change context within the retained governed scope. The common resumption set is the scope, work state, responsible participants, outstanding findings or blockers, and next action. The initial RigorLoop authoring profile defines additional context for authoring, implementation, verification, and review of a Change within one governed project; the applicable activity determines which context is needed. A field that is inapplicable to an activity is identified as such with a reason rather than populated with invented work or evidence. These definitions specify intended support and do not claim that every activity has an implemented record format. IR-001 owns durability of engineering definitions; this obligation addresses continuity of controlled work. It does not preserve unsaved conversation state or make a suggested next action authorize execution. The local operational-history extension adds the criteria attributed to SRC-LOCAL-OPERATIONAL-ANALYSIS; retained product contracts and old allocation evidence do not establish implementation or coverage of that extension.

acceptance_criteria: The handoff presents goal, scope and authority; governing requirement/design/plan references; current progress and remaining work; open issues and important rationale; relevant evidence; review standing; and the next action with reason and responsible participant. Each fact has one authoritative owner, not an independently editable duplicate.

After the originating session ends, another authorized participant can identify the next permitted step, its supporting basis and unresolved uncertainty from this handoff and bounded supporting reads.
Missing, conflicting or unavailable context is explicitly distinguished from not-applicable, not-run, no finding or approved. A suggested action never supplies its own execution authority.

Working state and equivalent evidence summaries may be explicitly replaced without preserving prior versions or recording every local action. Relevant scope, assessed basis, result, limitations and reporting source remain available for conclusions currently relied upon.
Open findings cannot disappear through omitted fields or shorter handoffs. An explicit attributable disposition is needed; resolved detail may later be compacted when no current reliance requires it.

Changes to material scope, blockers, evidence applicability, review standing or next action require a current handoff at the next dependent decision or transfer. Routine edits and intermediate test runs require no permanent record.
A restored backup identifies its retained state and unavailable later work; it does not renew authority or applicability. An unavailable store cannot be presented as an empty or completed Change.

Completion retains a compact account of outcome, reason, delivered scope, acceptance support and limitations. It is historical and is not continuously compared with the current repository; a later regression becomes a new linked problem or Change.

sources.locator: Resumable across sessions and agents; What it commits to
sources.basis: Current authoritative records carry task state so another participant can continue from the artifacts.
A Change controls engineering evolution, while current state remains understandable without replaying history.
